newsitem.title: GERMANY: Traders positive after DAX caps record week down.
newsitem.headline: Traders positive after DAX caps record week down.

text.p: German shares on Friday closed a lacklustre floor session down nearly half a percent but bounced back into positive territory in late trade, capping a record-breaking week.

The DAX-30 index ended bourse dealing down 18.10 points at 4,317.64 points -- about 90 off Wednesday's all-time high of 4,406.09 -- as most shares failed to gain much impetus from the strong dollar and its brief foray over 1.84 marks.
But the index bounced back in late trade to end IBIS computer trading at 4,368.54.
Dealers said Friday's pause shouldn't keep the DAX from continuing its upward charge until nearing resistance pegged at around 4,400 points.
"For next week I expect the market to continue rising," one trader said.

One of Friday's biggest losers was software group SAP AG, which fell almost five percent after a dramatic six-week rise, while Deutsche Bank AG, Commerzbonk AG and Siemens AG rose in the wake of positive earnings news.
SAP shares closed at 410.20, down 22.80 marks but still up 89 since June 13.

Analysts said the share fell after SAP told them that second-half growth was not expected to match rates in the first-half, when sales rose 51 percent to 2.4 billion marks and pretax profit 56 percent to 580 million marks.

"They had a very strong fourth quarter last year and so growth this year will be compared to a very high basis," said Hans Peter Wodniok at Credit Lyonnais. "They also have a major product introduction at the beginning of 1998, so some analysts may have thought the first quarter growth could be slower."
Deutsche Bank closed up 3.60 marks, or three percent, at 122.60, as WestLB raised estimates on Deutsche's earnings per share to 5.10 marks from 4.95 for 1997, and to 5.80 marks from 5.55 for 1998.
Commerzbank rose 1.20 marks, or 1.9 percent, to 63.20, on rising speculation that a foreign investor might be interested in the company in a wave of consolidaiton among German banks.

Siemens closed at 122.40 marks, up 1.60 or one percent, after presenting nine-month results to analysts Thursday night. The company reported a three percent gain in net income to 1.705 billion marks, even though it has forecast flat profit in the year ending Spetember 30.

The spectre of a possible interest rate rise haunted some market players, after the Bundesbank dropped a subtle hint to the markets that it could swing into action rapidly if a policy change were needed.

The central bank left its M3 target and all of its main interest rates unchanged after its regular policy meeting on Thursday, but kept markets guessing as to where its main money market rate would be set in two weeks' time.
"If an interest rate rise comes, then the DAX is around 500 points too high," one trader said, although another trader said that these fears were exaggerated.
